Low-Mileage Lamborghini Gallardo Spyder Hits the Used Car Market Stateside
13 photos
Photo: Cars&Bids
Did you know you can still buy a low-mileage Lamborghini Gallardo ? Takes this Spyder, which is now listed for grabs in the United States of America, and it is an almost flawless example.
The seller, who reportedly bought it in August 2025, adding some 1,000 miles (1,600 km) since, stated that it came from a private collection before he wrote his name on the dotted line, adding that he has enjoyed bring it back to driving condition. However, since he is now ready to move on to this “next automotive toy,” he put it up for sale, and this is one machine that deserves a lot of attention, especially if you are into the Gallardo.
It’s a well-documented example that has only 5,300 miles (8,500 km) under its belt since new. The 2008 Lamborghini Gallardo Spyder in question has zero modifications, which makes it even more desirable, and other than some wear on the interior switchgear, there is nothing else wrong with. The Carfax report reveals that the modern-classic Italian supercar hasn’t been involved in any accidents, and there are also no mileage discrepancies for extra peace of mind.
The supercar has a Nero Perseus black exterior paint finish on top of a Bianco Polar interior that combines white and black leather upholstery and some white stitching. The two-tone leather upholstery, a power-operated soft top, power adjustable and heated seats, a dual-zone climate control system, a basic infotainment system, a nose-lift system, 19-inch Callisto wheels are mentioned in the ad that we will link toward the end of this story.
Photo: Cars&Bids This open-top Lamborghini Gallardo had its clutch wear test performed in September 2026, revealing a 43.11 percent wear, and that is also when an airbag module was replaced. The tires were rotated in July 2026, and in June, it had its engine oil and filter changed. The brake fluid, coolant, and front differential fluids were flushed, the batter was replaced, the engine oil and filter were changed, and the tires were replaced in September 2025, when the car had 4,334 miles (6,975 km) under its belt.
You do know what powers this model, don’t you? If you said a naturally aspirated V10, then you certainly know your Italian supercars. The 5.0-liter engine was officially good for 513 brake horsepower (520 ps/382 kW) and 376 pound-feet (510 Nm) of torque. It had the ability to sprint to 60 mph (97 kph) in a hair over 4-second mark, and if you kept the right pedal pinned to the floor, then it would run out of breath at 195 mph (314 kph). A six-speed automated manual transmission delivers everything to all four wheels.
In addition to the car , the next owner will get one key, and the usual lecture consisting of the owner’s manuals, as well as some service records, and even the window sticker. The latter reveals that this machine was over a quarter of a million dollars back in the day. The MSRP was $253,745, to be more precise, and something like this is now worth a lot less. In fact, you will have to prepare between $100,000 and $140,000 for one of these in today’s used car market.
The six-speed manual variant can cost upward of $200,000, and ultra-low mileage examples, which have less than 10,000 miles (16,000 km) under their belts, typically sell for between $135,000 and upward of $170,000. And given that this 2008 Lamborghini Gallardo Spyder has a little over 5,000 miles, zero known flaws, and looks almost as good today as it did when it originally left the dealership nearly two decades ago, we reckon it will fetch a pretty penny when the gavel hits the table.
Photo: Cars&Bids Yep, it is advertised as part of an ongoing online auction, and you can find it on Cars&Bids. The event will end six days from now, next Monday, on November 2, 2026, and to little surprise, there is a reserve on it. At the time of writing, the highest bid was $50,000, and needless to say that the reserve hasn’t been met.
Before linking the ad, we will remind you that a little over 14,000 units of the Lamborghini Gallardo were made in total, with production spanning between 2003 and 2013. The Huracan’s predecessor, which, in turn, was replaced by the modern-day Temerario, was initially designed by Fabrizio Giugiaro at Italdesign, with Luc Donckerwolke signing the final design, and Walter de Silva leaving his mark on the facelifted iteration.
Coupe and convertible versions of the supercar were made, and some of them were offered with pure rear-wheel drive. The model shared its nuts and bolts with the original Audi R8 , and while the pre-facelift came with a 5.0-liter naturally aspirated V10, the mid-cycle refresh brought the 5.2-liter mill that everyone knows.
Now, you can check out this Lamborghini Gallardo Spyder here on the quoted website, and before clicking that link, feel free to tell us how much this thing is worth to you.
